question.problem: Using the extended Euclidean algorithm, compute integers $u$ and $v$ such that $53u+24v=\text{gcd}(53,24).$ What is the value of $u+v?$
question.worked_solution:
We will use the extended Euclidean algorithm. First, we apply the forward reduction:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}53 & = & 24\cdot 2 & + & 5 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 24 & = & 5\cdot 4 & + & 4 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 5 & = & 4\cdot 1 & + & 1\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, $\text{gcd}(53,24)=1.$

Solving for the remainders (the rightmost terms) in the equations above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}5 & =53-24\cdot 2 \\ 4 & =24-5\cdot 4 \\ 1 & =5-4.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we back-substitute:

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & =5-4 \\  & =5-(24-5\cdot 4) \\  & =5\cdot 5-24 \\  & =[53-24\cdot 2]\cdot 5-24 \\  & =53\cdot 5-24\cdot 11 \\  & =53\cdot 5+24\cdot (-11)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $u=5$ and $v=-11.$

Finally, 

$$
u+v=5+(-11)=-6.
$$
